summary: Crawford County tower on a five-acre towersite, erected 1940 by the Missouri Conservation Commission; upkeep recorded to 1978; current status not in the sources read.

facts.agency: Missouri Conservation Commission, later Missouri Department of Conservation

events.note: Five acres acquired by the Conservation Commission for the purpose of erecting a fire tower.
Commission authorized a dwelling and garage for the tower (Sullivan News, Sept. 28, 1939); work had started by Sept. 29 (Thayer News).
68-foot steel tower erected on a 5-acre towersite (Commission report). A 1939 report had given 67 feet.
Fire watcher Merrell Stone returned from war and resumed work at the Leasburg tower (Sullivan News, Sept. 13, 1945).
Dwelling completely remodeled, two bedrooms and a bathroom added (FY 1964-65).
Major repairs to the tower residence (FY 1967-68).
New furnace at the residence and a new tower entrance road (FY 1972-73).
Two-room addition and a new entrance road (FY 1973-74).
Doors repaired and a new water heater installed at the tower residence.
New field drain at the towersite (FY 1977-78).

corrections.why: The record's 20.4 m is 67 feet, the figure from a 1939 report of towers being erected. The 1940 report of the completed tower gives 68 feet, which is 20.7 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 67 feet (1939 report of towers being erected) and 68 feet (1940 report of the completed tower). The story and facts use 68 feet, the completed-tower figure.

notes_for_editor: Only one source, a transcription of annual reports and 1939-1945 newspaper items on the Central US Lookouts page. No source found says whether the tower still stands, who owns the site now, or whether it is open to the public, so status and access stay unknown. The MDC area page guessed at /discover-nature/places/leasburg-towersite returned 404. The Central Region towersite plan on archive.org does not list Leasburg. A Southeast Region towersite plan was not checked. Height 67 vs 68 ft is the main conflict; the story uses 68 ft.
